feedback.problem: Let $x=[\begin{aligned}12 \\ 6 \\ -6 \\ 12\end{aligned}]$ and $a=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 6 \\ -6 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$ If $x=y+z,$ where $y\in \text{Span}{a}$ and $z⊥\text{Span}{a},$ then $z=$
feedback.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14066555/assets/d887852fe51f08cb7296437e69b6a9632721cfd155558e6abf9a99b4f59f7ad6.png)

First, we find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto $\text{Span}{a}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{a}\,x & =\frac{a\cdot x}{a\cdot a}a \\  & =\frac{2\cdot 12+6\cdot 6+(-6)\cdot (-6)+2\cdot 12}{{2}^{2}+{6}^{2}+(-6)^{2}+{2}^{2}}a \\  & =\frac{24+36+36+24}{4+36+36+4}a \\  & =\frac{120}{80}a \\  & =\frac{3}{2}a \\  & =\frac{3}{2}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 6 \\ -6 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 9 \\ -9 \\ 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we get the following: 

$$
\begin{aligned}y & ={\text{proj}}_{a}\,x=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 9 \\ -9 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\ z & =x-{\text{proj}}_{a}\,x=[\begin{aligned}12 \\ 6 \\ -6 \\ 12\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 9 \\ -9 \\ 3\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}9 \\ -3 \\ 3 \\ 9\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that $y\in \text{Span}{a}$ and $z⊥\text{Span}{a},$ as shown in the picture above.

In conclusion, $z=[\begin{aligned}9 \\ -3 \\ 3 \\ 9\end{aligned}].$
